god_relations.note: Djedi knows where knowledge associated with Thoth’s sanctuary is kept.
Djedi proclaims that Ra fathered Ruddjedet’s three future royal children.

god_relations.myth: Nitocris gains magical Egyptian divine associations
god_relations.note: Fate/Grand Order associates Nitocris’s magical powers and pharaonic identity with Horus.

god_relations.myth: Nitocris gains underworld and jackal associations
god_relations.note: Fate/Grand Order associates Nitocris with Anubis through jackal imagery and underworld powers.
The historical Khaemwaset served as Ptah's sem-priest and high priest at Memphis.
Ptah's amulets and magical books restore or protect Setne during his struggle.

god_relations.myth: Theft of the Book of Thoth
god_relations.note: Setne removes the divine book belonging to Thoth from Naneferkaptah's tomb.

god_relations.myth: The Book of Thoth's second spell
god_relations.note: The book taken by Setne reveals Re with the Ennead, without personal dialogue.
Setne gives Isis an ox, goose, wine, burnt offering, and libation.
Setne gives Harpocrates offerings beside Isis before searching the Coptos cemetery.
Tabubu identifies herself through her father's priestly service to Bastet; Setne never meets the goddess.

god_relations.myth: Ahwere's history of the divine book
god_relations.note: Ahwere invokes Neith's curse while addressing Setne, but he has no direct encounter with her.

god_relations.myth: Journey through seven halls of Amenti
god_relations.note: Setne sees Osiris enthroned over judgment in Amenti.
Khaemwaset's statue bears a prayer to Osiris as an act of cultic devotion.
Setne witnesses Anubis participating in judgment beside Osiris.
Setne witnesses Thoth recording the weighing of the dead's deeds.
Setne witnesses the judgment system in which Ammit destroys condemned souls.
Setne hears Si-Osire address the Nubian envoy concerning Amun's power.
Khaemwaset's statue bears a prayer to Atum.

god_relations.myth: Embedded contest of Egyptian and Nubian magicians
god_relations.note: Setne hears the embedded magician invoke Atum in an oath.
The historical Khaemwaset venerates Imhotep on a monument bearing the epithet son of Ptah.
Khaemwaset officiates in funerary rituals and burials for Apis as a divine manifestation.
Sinuhe praises Montu after killing the champion and later invokes him for Senusret.
Sinuhe invokes Ra as loving Senusret and inspiring worldwide fear of him.
Sinuhe invokes Amun to bless Senusret.
Sinuhe invokes Horus to bless Senusret, whom the tale calls Horus who seizes.
Sinuhe invokes Hathor to love and sustain Senusret.
Sinuhe invokes Atum together with his Ennead to bless Senusret.
Sinuhe invokes Sopdu as an eastern god of effective power.
Sinuhe invokes Nut in the divine assembly blessing Senusret.
Bata invokes sunrise as the divine forum revealing justice between the brothers.
The gods pity Bata and acknowledge that Anubis has avenged him.

god_relations.myth: Bata named Bull of the Ennead
god_relations.note: The assembled gods confer upon Bata the epithet Bull of the Ennead.
Khnum fashions a divinely beautiful wife for Bata at Re-Horakhty’s command.
A Jumilhac vignette depicts bull-form Bata carrying the mummy of Osiris.

god_relations.myth: Wenamun’s mission to obtain timber for Amun’s sacred bark
god_relations.note: Wenamun serves Amun’s institution, carries his dispatches, and claims the god commissioned and protected his mission.

Ahwere.myth: Ahwere's history of the divine book
Ahwere.note: Ahwere narrates the book's fatal history and warns Setne within the tomb.
Setne retrieves Ahwere's body and transfers it to Naneferkaptah's Memphis tomb.

Amenemhat I.note: Sinuhe serves the royal household; Amenemhat’s death precipitates his unexplained flight.

Amun-of-the-Road.note: The portable divine image accompanies Wenamun and is presented as Amun’s divine envoy.

Atum’s Ennead.note: Sinuhe collectively invokes Atum’s Ennead to bless Senusret.

Bedivere.note: Nitocris and Bedivere participate in rescue, combat, and alliance episodes in Camelot.

Hassan of the Hundred Faces.note: Nitocris and Hassan participate in rescue, combat, or alliance episodes in Camelot.

Horus the Easterner.note: Sinuhe invokes this eastern aspect or title of Horus for Senusret.

Horwerra.note: Sinuhe invokes this obscure composite deity in the blessing of Senusret.

Khephren.myth: Nitocris and Khephren rule hybrid mummies underground
Khephren.note: Lovecraft makes Nitocris Khephren’s subterranean consort and fellow ruler of hybrid mummies.

Lady of All.note: Feminine divine titles appear in Sinuhe’s prayer and the royal women’s intercession.

Lady of the Cavern.note: Sinuhe invokes this uncertainly identified goddess by title in the royal blessing.

Lion King.myth: Opposition to the Lion King in Camelot
Lion King.note: Nitocris participates in opposition to the Lion King during the Camelot narrative.

Mash Kyrielight.note: Nitocris and Mash participate in rescue, combat, and alliance episodes in Camelot.

Medjed.myth: Nitocris gains magical Egyptian divine associations
Medjed.note: Fate/Grand Order links Nitocris with Medjed through magical powers and imagery.

Merenre Nemtyemsaf II.myth: Modern identification of Nitocris’s murdered royal brother
Merenre Nemtyemsaf II.note: Modern genealogies identify him as the brother whom Nitocris succeeds and avenges.
Modern popular genealogies make him Nitocris’s husband or sister-husband.

Merib.note: Setne retrieves Merib's body and reunites him with his dead parents.

Min-Horus.note: Sinuhe invokes Min-Horus amid the hill-lands.

Naneferkaptah.myth: Theft of the Book of Thoth
Naneferkaptah.note: Setne takes the divine book from Naneferkaptah's tomb despite his warning.
Setne plays Naneferkaptah, whose victories drive him progressively into the ground.
Naneferkaptah apparently engineers Setne's humiliating illusion, though the precise mechanism remains uncertain.

Naneferkaptah.myth: Restitution of the Book of Thoth
Naneferkaptah.note: Setne returns the stolen book and reunites Naneferkaptah with his dead family.

Ozymandias.note: Nitocris serves as Ozymandias’s ally and subordinate in the Camelot narrative.
Ozymandias acts as Nitocris’s superior during the Camelot narrative.

Pre-Harakhty.note: He answers Bata’s appeal by creating crocodile-filled water between the brothers.
He commands Khnum to fashion a wife for the solitary Bata.

Ra-Horakhty.note: Setne hears Egypt described as Ra-Horakhty's footstool or beautiful horizon.

Re.note: Setne's stolen book reveals Re and his Ennead; Setne is later associated with Re's radiance.

Senusret I.note: Sinuhe accompanies the army commanded by Senusret before fleeing Egypt.
Senusret pardons Sinuhe, recalls him from exile and restores his courtly status.
Senusret grants Sinuhe a pyramid-chapel, statue, funerary personnel and endowed estate.

Seth.note: Local theology identifies or closely associates the divine bull-form Bata with Seth.

Si-Osire.note: Setne fathers the miraculous Si-Osire, temporary reincarnation of Hor son of Pa-neshe.

Si-Osire.myth: Journey through seven halls of Amenti
Si-Osire.note: Si-Osire guides Setne through Amenti and teaches that deeds outweigh funerary splendor.
Si-Osire saves Setne and Egypt by reading the sealed letter and defeating its Nubian author.
Setne continually makes offerings and libations to Hor son of Pa-neshe's spirit.

Sobek-Ra.note: Sinuhe invokes Sobek-Ra within the divine assembly blessing Senusret.

Sokar-Osiris.note: Setne learns that souls with balanced deeds are assigned to Sokar-Osiris's service.

Tabubu.note: Setne coercively propositions Tabubu and accepts her escalating demands for sexual access.
Tabubu subjects Setne to an illusion of dispossession, child murder, and sexual humiliation.

The Seven Hathors.note: They inspect Bata’s newly fashioned wife and predict her death by knife.

deified Old Kingdom Djedi.note: Modern scholars controversially identify the Westcar magician with a same-named deified man.
